chunks: Al-Abbas and Al-Hasan ibn Ali together from Ali from Fadala from Mu'awiya from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'The people of Mecca complete the prayer at Arafat.' He said, 'Woe to them or woe to them! And which journey is harder than it? No, no, they do not complete (the prayer).'

key_terms.يُتِمُّونَ: They complete (prayer, i.e., praying four rak'ahs instead of two)

ai.seo_question: Do pilgrims shorten or complete their prayers at Arafat during Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refutes the prevailing practice of the people of Mecca who completed their prayers at Arafat, asserting that Arafat is a place of travel (*safar*) rather than a permanent residence. He emphasizes the severity of this error with the phrase 'Woe to them,' reinforcing the Shia jurisprudential view that the pilgrim's status as a traveler persists at Arafat, thus requiring the shortening (*qasr*) of the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs.
